name: Egga (Egyptian Baked Egg Dish)

cookwares.name: or nonstick skillet; whisk; flexible spatula; 9- by-13-inch baking dish

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, divided, plus more for greasing
finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves, tender stems
finely chopped fresh Italian parsley leaves, tender stems
finely chopped fresh dill leaves, tender stems
Egyptian pickled green olives, pitted and coarsely chopped or sliced

instructions.primary_message: Finely chop the yellow onions. Seed and dice the plum tomato. Cut the russet potato into 1/2-inch pieces.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium yellow onions
1 medium plum tomato
1 medium russet potato

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

In a medium stainless steel, cast iron, carbon steel, or nonstick skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium-low heat. Add onions and season with salt and black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions have softened and are light golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Transfer onions to a plate or bowl and set aside.

In the same skillet (no need to wipe clean), melt 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat. Add chopped tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes have softened and released their juices, about 2 minutes. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until juices have reduced and tomato has darkened slightly, 3 more minutes. Transfer tomato to plate or bowl with onions; set aside.

In the same skillet (no need to wipe clean), melt 3 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Add chopped potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are light golden brown and tender, 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from heat; set aside to cool slightly.

In small bowl, whisk flour and baking powder to combine; set aside. In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs, milk, salt, black pepper, ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, sweet paprika (if using), red pepper flakes (if using), and ground nutmeg to combine. Whisk vigorously until mixture is frothy and pale yellow, 3 to 5 minutes. Whisk in flour and baking powder to combine.
Using a flexible spatula, fold in onions, tomatoes, potatoes, cilantro, parsley, dill, pickled olives, and sun-dried tomatoes (if using).

Lightly grease a 9-by-33-cm baking dish. Pour egg mixture into dish and bake until top is puffed, set, and lightly golden, and a toothpick or cake tester inserted in the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Turn off the oven and let it cool slightly for 5 minutes. Using oven mitts or hot pads, remove dish from oven, place a wide serving dish over the baking dish and, using a kitchen towel if necessary, carefully flip the baking dish to invert the egga onto the serving dish.
Serve with pickles and warm aish baladi (Egyptian flatbread) or pitas, if desired.

schema_metadata.keywords: egga, egga recipe, egyptian egga recipe

description: Packed with softened onions, fresh herbs, and seasoned with warm spices, egga—a baked egg dish—is Egypt's answer to the weekend brunch casserole.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1/2 teaspoon sweet paprika, optional; 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes or Aleppo pepper, optional; 2 sun-dried tomatoes (5 g), optional; Pickles, such as Egyptian pickled olives, cucumbers, or turnips, for serving, optional; Warm aish baladi (Egyptian flatbread) or pita, for serving, optional

Make-ahead and storage: The onions, tomato, and potato can be cooked up to 3 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. When ready to assemble, proceed with step 5 of recipe.
Once cooled, the egga can be refrigerated in an airtight container up to 3 days or tightly wrapped in plastic and frozen for up to 1 month. When ready to serve, reheat in oven or toaster oven at 175°C (350°F) until warmed through, about 15 minutes.
author: Nermine Mansour
